items.title: Pudu Robotics rides the tidal wave of China’s AI revolution
items.summary: Pudu Robotics has grown into a billion-dollar company by developing a broad portfolio of commercial service and industrial robots. The company's success is driven by its "One Brain, Multiple Embodiments" strategy, which allows robots to share common AI and software foundations. Pudu is expanding globally, operating in over 85 countries and having shipped over 130,000 robots worldwide. A significant portion of its revenue comes from commercial cleaning robots, which account for over 70% of 2025 revenue. Intense competition among Chinese robotics companies is reshaping the global industry.

Pudu Robotics is currently expanding globally, maintaining operations in more than eighty-five countries and having shipped over one hundred thirty thousand robots internationally. items.title: Motion demonstrates Galbot S1 palletizing at Slush summit
items.summary: Motion showcased the Galbot S1 palletizing robot at the Industrial Renaissance Summit in Helsinki on November 19, 2026. The robot weighs 320 kilograms with a 50 kilogram payload and uses lidar to slow down near people. Motion also presented MotionOS, a software platform built on Google Cloud and Gemini for task qualification, training, and remote support. The company leases its robots, and its customer base includes food and beverage, heavy industry, and warehouse logistics. The presentation emphasized how robots address labor shortages in industries like logistics and manufacturing.

items.title: Foundation unveils Phantom MKII humanoid for industry and defense
items.summary: Foundation Future Industries has released the Phantom MKII humanoid, a second-generation robot with a Cortex II control system, for heavy industry and defense applications. This humanoid can navigate adverse weather conditions while carrying 200 pounds and is intended for use on construction sites and in factories. The company is considering arming its robots if requested by the U.S. military, with a rationale that armed ground robots could reduce drone reliance. This launch follows disputed reports regarding the potential military use of earlier Phantom models. Founder Sankaet Pathak disputed claims of direct military supply negotiations, describing earlier discussions as merely exploratory.

items.title: Humyn Labs raises $47M to collect real-world data for robotics

items.title: From Commercial Scale to Embodied Intelligence: The Next Challenge for Robotics
items.summary: Greater robotic capability must translate into consistent, scalable, and reliable performance in real-world commercial environments. Pudu Robotics leverages experience from large-scale commercial deployments to tackle this challenge by pursuing embodied intelligence through a "One Brain, Multiple Embodiments" strategy. This strategy uses PuduFM and PuduAgent to create a shared foundation for extending AI capabilities across diverse robot forms. The company is expanding its portfolio from commercial settings into residential and outdoor applications, such as lawn care robots. Ultimately, the next challenge for robotics is making intelligence reliably work in the physical world to create tangible value.

items.title: Welcome, PHD Hand!
items.summary: A printable humanoid dexterous hand prototype was developed by researchers at the New Jersey Institute of Technology. It utilizes an affordable, printable mechanical design with five fingers employing linkages and flexible hinges. The mechanism is driven by miniature servo motors without gear trains, constructed primarily from PETG and TPU. The prototype weighs 0.5 kilograms and is 200 millimeters in size, with a Humanoid Guide score of 4 out of 10. The project aims to promote accessible fabrication by releasing the design files openly for educational and community use.

items.title: ROS Discourse General: Fault correlation for ROS 2: one cause, many faults (and what automotive does about it)
items.summary: Robot startup and chain reactions often present multiple reported faults stemming from a single underlying issue. The example demonstrated how a single lidar connection failure led to several cascading errors in ROS 2 nodes like costmap and navigation. A correlation rule was developed to link the lidar fault as the root cause to subsequent symptoms like costmap timeouts and goal rejections. This rule utilized a time window to associate related events and mute symptoms once the cause was identified. The system suggests using fault history to propose correlation rules, although human approval is still needed for implementation.
items.audio_script: From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: Fault correlation for ROS 2: one cause, many faults (and what automotive does about it)" details a method for correlating faults within the Robot Operating System 2 framework, demonstrating that a single underlying issue can cause multiple reported errors in subsequent nodes. A correlation rule was developed to link a specific lidar connection failure as the root cause to cascading errors such as costmap timeouts and goal rejections. This process utilized a time window to associate related events and mute the symptoms once the initial fault was identified. The system suggests using fault history to propose these correlation rules, although human approval remains necessary before implementation. This research provides a mechanism for improved diagnostic accuracy in complex robotic systems. The findings indicate a pathway toward more robust fault detection in autonomous systems.

items.title: Kawasaki Robotics launches F Series S-type controller with integrated safety and cybersecurity
items.summary: Kawasaki Robotics launched the F Series Controller S-type, which integrates safety software and cybersecurity functions with the existing F Series platform. This controller, available from November 2026, helps machine builders comply with evolving European regulations while protecting investments. It includes standard CoreCubic-S Lite safety software and built-in cybersecurity features like user authentication and secure communications. The S-type allows for upgrades from existing F Series B-type controllers and supports optional energy recovery technology. This development addresses new regulations like the EU Machinery Regulation and the Cyber Resilience Act.

items.title: Imagry and Endera partner to bring American-made autonomous buses to US transit
items.summary: Imagry and Endera partnered to deliver the first Buy America-compliant autonomous buses and shuttles for US public transit. This collaboration combines Imagry’s Level 4 autonomous driving system with Endera’s American-built vehicles. The goal is to allow transit operators nationwide to purchase self-driving options using federal transit funds without needing a Buy America waiver. This initiative aims to support American manufacturing and cost-effective autonomous public transport. The technology promises to improve accessibility and reduce congestion by serving underserved areas and making public transit more efficient.

items.title: Rockwell Automation acquiring mobile robot maker AGILOX
items.summary: Rockwell Automation agreed to acquire AGILOX, an Austrian developer of autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), to expand its AMR business. This acquisition is expected to more than double Rockwell's AMR business and complement its existing OTTO Motors portfolio. AGILOX will join Rockwell’s Intelligent Devices operating segment, bringing its expertise in AMRs to the company. The deal aims to combine OTTO's North American presence with AGILOX's European customer base. The acquisition also marks an exit for global investor Carlyle, which previously invested in AGILOX.

items.title: Hidonix launches Hido II autonomous rover for indoor mapping
items.summary: Hidonix Industries has launched the Hido II autonomous rover to automate indoor mapping and geospatial data collection. The rover integrates autonomous navigation, advanced sensing, and a modular robotic arm to collect geomagnetic and spatial data. It navigates complex indoor environments, including stairs and uneven surfaces, following predefined routes without constant manual control. Testing demonstrated that Hido II reduced mapping time by 50% and achieved positioning errors five times lower than manual collection. This system is part of Hidonix's ION platform for commercial spatial intelligence and robotics.

items.title: Soft exosuit makes it easier to stand up
items.summary: Researchers at the Technical University of Munich developed a soft, lightweight exosuit to assist elderly individuals in standing up from chairs and walking more efficiently. The suit uses artificial tendons and sensors that, guided by machine learning, provide support at the hip during the movement. Testing showed that participants achieved more sit-and-stand cycles in less time and experienced reduced metabolic cost during walking. Users reported feeling in control of their movements despite the robotic assistance, indicating a high degree of perceived autonomy. The design allows the suit to be worn comfortably over normal clothing, aiming to support independence for older adults and those in rehabilitation.

items.title: This featherweight, flying robot carries its own sensors and computers
items.summary: Researchers developed a flapping-wing microrobot with onboard sensors and computation, making it sensory and compute autonomous. This robot achieved a lift-to-weight ratio of 1.9, allowing it to carry a 244-milligram electronics package for sensing and computation. The system uses an inertial measurement unit, optical flow sensor, and time-of-flight sensor for rapid position estimation without external motion capture. A novel sensing algorithm allows the robot to calculate its orientation and position quickly, achieving positional accuracy comparable to offboard cameras. This technology shows promise for applications like precision agriculture and industrial surveillance.

items.title: ROS Discourse General: ROS 2 on macOS: measured topic rates for each RMW, a Fast DDS shared-memory pitfall, and tuned presets
items.summary: Benchmarking ROS 2 RMW implementations on macOS revealed significant performance differences based on the transport used. Fast DDS's default shared-memory (SHM) transport on macOS suffers from a polling tick delay, leading to message bursts and high latency. Cyclone DDS with iceoryx offered the fastest performance, achieving up to 200 kHz rates with very low latency. Zenoh proved to be a good all-rounder, particularly when batching is disabled for high rates and shared memory is enabled for large messages. Optimal configurations involve selecting RMWs based on message size and required throughput.
items.audio_script:
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: ROS 2 on macOS: measured topic rates for each RMW, a Fast DDS shared-memory pitfall, and tuned presets" details the performance measurement of ROS 2 Real-Time Middleware implementations on macOS and presents specific findings regarding transport performance. Benchmarking of various RMW implementations on macOS revealed significant performance variations dependent on the transport layer utilized. The investigation examined the performance of Fast DDS, Cyclone DDS with iceoryx, and Zenoh. The results indicated that Fast DDS's default shared-memory transport on macOS introduced a polling tick delay, resulting in message bursts and elevated latency. Cyclone DDS with iceoryx demonstrated the highest performance, achieving rates up to 200 kHz with minimal latency. Zenoh provided a balanced performance profile, particularly when batching was disabled for high rates and shared memory enabled for larger messages.

These measurements guide the selection of appropriate RMWs based on message size and required throughput for system design. Future development should focus on utilizing these transport-specific optimizations for high-performance ROS deployments.

items.title: Build Training-Ready Physical AI Datasets with Two Prompts in NVIDIA Cosmos
items.summary: NVIDIA Cosmos provides a platform with the Data Factory (CDF) to accelerate data curation, processing, and synthetic data generation for physical AI. This platform utilizes coding agents and blueprints to orchestrate workflows for creating diverse training datasets. Five use cases include generating autonomous vehicle scenarios, augmenting images and videos, creating rare event videos, and generating defect images. Using this method, NVIDIA demonstrated up to 60x faster and 45x cheaper dataset assembly compared to traditional methods. The system leverages core agent skills like Auto Labeling and Augmentation to turn hard-to-collect data gaps into manageable generation jobs.

items.title: BiCAT: Bimanual Coordination Action Tokenization
items.summary: BiCAT addresses the challenge of modeling bimanual coordination in vision-language-action models by proposing a novel action tokenization method. It shares a common motion representation across both arms while using symmetric cross-arm attention and a joint decoder to condition each arm's tokens. This approach allows the policy to predict both arm tokens in parallel, generating the left arm first and then the right arm conditioned on it. Evaluation across various tasks showed BiCAT significantly improved success, especially in coordination-heavy tasks, with minimal latency. The results suggest that the action tokenizer is an effective mechanism for modeling bimanual coordination.

items.title: Learning and Control in Physically Coupled Dynamical Systems
items.summary: A compact robotic platform called TAG is introduced to study learning and control in physically coupled dynamical systems. TAG integrates an actively tilted maze board and a top-mounted rotary inverted pendulum that physically interact with each other. The study addresses the challenge of accounting for one subsystem's dynamics on the learning process of the other. Complementary model-based and model-free reinforcement learning methods are used to learn control policies for the maze and pendulum. Experimental results show that both policies successfully control their respective systems despite the physical coupling.

items.title: RageVLA: Augmentation-Trained Perception and Action for State-of-the-Art Robustness on LIBERO
items.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models struggle with robustness on LIBERO, particularly when objects move or instructions change. RageVLA addresses this by decoupling the task dependencies in the data and policy. It uses a perception engine on frozen DINOv3 features and TinyCLIP embeddings to provide the action model with decoupled scene and instruction views. A flow-matching diffusion transformer is then trained from scratch on this input. RageVLA achieves state-of-the-art performance on LIBERO-PRO, demonstrating robustness to object position changes.

items.title: RESCUE Jumper: A Centimeter-Scale Rolling and Jumping Robot for Search and Rescue
items.summary: RESCUE Jumper is a centimeter-scale mobile robot designed for search and rescue operations in confined spaces. It combines ground rolling with jumping to overcome obstacles that exceed its rolling capability. The robot uses its actuators to roll forward and reverse motion to wind a spring steel tail for jumping. Winding speed controls the jump direction, resulting in jumps with heights up to 9.2 cm. The work provides a model and experimental results for developing jump mechanisms in space-constrained robots.

items.title: Learning the Dynamics of Deformable Linear Objects Through Coupled Oscillators for Bimanual Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: The research proposes $\Phi$-CON, a model combining a floating-base coupled oscillator network (FBCON) with a learned affine diffeomorphism ($\Phi$) to learn the dynamics of deformable linear objects (DLOs). This approach explicitly models the mechanical response of objects, moving beyond simplified deformation models. A model-based proportional-derivative (PD) controller is designed using this structure to ensure closed-loop stability and convergence. Evaluation on simulations and real-world robot experiments shows the method significantly reduces error and improves endpoint regulation compared to model-free baselines.

items.title: Panini- Feasible Grammar For Robot Designs
items.summary: A typed production grammar is introduced to generate both manipulation skills and robot morphologies using case-role relations and parameter inheritance. A geometric realization map translates grammar composition into transformations in SE(3), which shows a measurable defect when inheritance is active. The grammar results allow for geometrically coordinated limb placement, achieving 95% jointly feasible edits. A cross-entropy search method, PANINI, was explored over grammar-based representations. This work demonstrates that typed grammars enhance interpretability and geometric coordination in robot design.

items.title: LuxTac: A Flexible, Scalable, and Open-Source Optical Taxel Array with Distributed Three-Axis Force Sensing for Tactile Robot Learning
items.summary: LuxTac is a flexible, scalable, and open-source optical taxel array designed for tactile robot learning. It consists of a 3.5 mm thick array where each taxel acts as a digital RGBC light-to-digital converter. The array can sense normal force using a plain gel cartridge, and shear force by using a cartridge with colored walls that encode shear information. Distributed three-axis force sensing is achieved across the array, showing strong correlation with indenter forces. Incorporating LuxTac pressure readings into a policy significantly improves peg-in-hole success.

items.title: SPICE: Stochastic Policy for Interaction in Cluttered Environments
items.summary: SPICE is a tactile-conditioned diffusion policy designed for robotic reaching through dense plant canopies using only tactile sensing for environmental feedback. It demonstrates three capabilities: moving through foliage, maneuvering around stems, and manipulating obstructing branches. Evaluation across 180 real-robot trials showed that spatial tactile information significantly improved branch maneuvering success compared to other baselines. SPICE achieved 95% success in branch maneuvering and 87.5% zero-shot transfer success on unseen plants. These results highlight the potential of tactile-conditioned generative policies for complex physical interactions in visually occluded environments.

items.title: Recoverability, Not Invariance: Certified Safety for Robots at the Limits of Performance
items.summary: Safety certification in robotics should focus on recoverability rather than forward invariance, especially at performance limits where models are uncertain. The paper introduces recoverability, a contraction-theoretic concept, to certify a robot's ability to switch to a trusted recovery mode. This approach guarantees exponential convergence to the recovery mode, even with model errors and disturbances. A switching-time program is derived to dictate when to switch, ensuring safety and optimality. Validation in simulations and hardware tests demonstrated this method's superiority over invariance-based safety filters for aggressive maneuvers.

items.title: How Uncertain Is My Action? Self-Correcting Visual Planning with Frozen World Models
items.summary: A frozen latent world model combined with sampling-based model predictive control forms a visual planning method. The system can reverse the model to quantify actuation shifts by comparing predictions with actual observations. A specific score detects these shifts, estimates them, and compensates the planner when an anomaly is detected. This self-correction method significantly improved success rates in vision-based tasks compared to other adaptation methods. Ultimately, the frozen world model acts as a filter to test action validity and correct planning failures.
